# Morning digest

**Status:** specced, not built.
**Article:** [Finding Your Next Job, with AI](/aging-well/next-job.md) — plan two, "the target."
**Precedent:** [`budget-from-statements`](/aging-well/budget-from-statements.md) — a browser tab, your own files, nothing uploaded.

## What it does

Pulls postings from employer application-tracking systems' own public JSON
feeds — Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby — for a reader-curated list of companies,
ranks them against a one-page profile with a short LLM call, and writes a
dated Markdown digest: new postings since yesterday, each with a one-line
fit note.

## Why this source, not LinkedIn

The point of this tool is what it *doesn't* touch. Reading a company's own
public ATS feed is unauthenticated, rate-limit-free and outside any
platform's terms of service — unlike scraping or automating LinkedIn, Indeed
or Glassdoor, which the
[GitHub research](/aging-well/research/github-open-source.md#1-auto-apply--application-bots)
documents as a real account-restriction risk (LinkedIn reported flagging
23.5M automated sessions in one 2026 quarter). It's also where roles that
never get boosted on the big boards actually sit — the closest open-source
analogue is [freehire.me](https://freehire.me), which does this at scale and
is worth linking as the hosted alternative for a reader who wants it built
already.

## What it needs

- A reader-maintained list of companies and their ATS type (most
  Greenhouse/Lever/Ashby job boards expose a documented public JSON
  endpoint — `boards-api.greenhouse.io/v1/boards/<company>/jobs`, for
  example).
- The ranking step reuses the eight-line evaluation prompt from the article
  (role, requirement fit citing `evidence.md`, seniority match, salary as a
  multiple, AI-disclosure note, likely interview questions, outreach
  candidates, fit score) — this is a fixed prompt, not new design.
- A way to run daily without a server: a scheduled browser tab, a bookmarklet,
  or a small script the reader runs themselves (`cron` is fine for a reader
  comfortable with it; needs a no-terminal path too).

## Open

- Whether ranking needs a hosted-model API key from the reader, or can run
  against a local model for readers who'd rather nothing left the machine.
- How large a company list is worth curating before the source list itself
  becomes the maintenance burden.
